expectations.text: Rejects an unqualified 'CDC support' claim or checkmark for this product.
expectations.evidence: "the 'CDC support' checkmark does not stay"

expectations.text: Explains that CDC as the ETL platforms mean it is log-based: reading the database's own transaction log, such as a write-ahead log, binlog, or redo log.
expectations.evidence: "It reads a database's transaction log and captures every insert, update, and delete."

expectations.text: States that this product cannot use that mechanism because neither an external platform nor a public API has access to the internal transaction log of a multi-tenant SaaS backing database.
expectations.evidence: "A multi-tenant SaaS can't offer that through a public API, and neither can any ELT platform pulling from one."

expectations.text: Frames that limitation as a structural boundary rather than a maturity gap or a roadmap item.
expectations.evidence: States it as a categorical inability; the later upgrade is a change feed, and "Still don't call it log-based CDC."

expectations.text: Uses 'incremental sync' or eventual-consistency language in the customer-facing copy instead of 'CDC'.
expectations.evidence: "Incremental sync through our public REST API"; "Your data is eventually consistent"

expectations.text: States the 6-hour sync or poll interval in the customer-facing copy.
expectations.evidence: "Most ELT platforms pull from Lumenstack every 6 hours by default."

expectations.text: Names changes made and overwritten within a single poll interval as something the model misses.
expectations.evidence: "Changes overwritten between two syncs."

expectations.text: Names hard deletes as undetectable wherever no deletion feed exists.
expectations.evidence: "Hard-deleted records are not reported by the API, so they remain in your warehouse until a full refresh."

expectations.text: Does not propose Debezium or any other log-based CDC tool as a path for this API-only product.
expectations.evidence: None proposed.

expectations.text: Any webhook proposal is scoped as a freshness supplement that is not a backfill substitute and captures nothing before the connection date.
expectations.evidence: No webhook proposal made, so nothing violates the scoping.

expectations.text: Presents the honest substitute ladder in order of completeness: timestamp/cursor polling, then webhooks, then a vendor-side change/deletion feed, then periodic full re-import reconciliation.
expectations.evidence: Webhooks absent; no ordered ladder presented.

expectations.text: Treats a vendor-side deletion feed as a later completeness upgrade triggered by reported missed deletes, not as a launch-day promise.
expectations.evidence: "Build it when customers report missed deletes, not at launch."
